name: Charles Hector McFadyen
context: Charles Hector McFadyen (1892–1965) served in the First World War and later led the Commonwealth Department of Shipping and Transport. The family identifies him as the compiler of these scrapbooks. Wikipedia cites two volumes held by the McFadyen family; that citation is corroborating context, not an independent authentication of every artifact.

name: P. M. Haydon
context: The printed caption on Book 1, scan 010 names Rev. P. M. Haydon as the new Canberra parish priest. The handwritten annotation recalls his standing in Queanbeyan and Canberra. This is context from the scrapbook; the identification has not been checked against an external authority.

name: T. M. Dunleavy
context: The printed caption on Book 1, scan 010 names Rev. T. M. Dunleavy, assistant pastor at Queanbeyan. A handwritten note connects him with boxer Jack Dunleavy. That relationship is the compiler’s assertion and awaits independent confirmation.

name: Edith Cavell
context: A handwritten caption on Book 1, scan 010 describes a stone marking the place in Brussels where nurse Edith Cavell was shot. The caption supplies the association; this website has not independently verified the location of the photograph.

name: F. G. Ward
context: The handwritten portrait caption on Book 1, scan 010 identifies Canon F. G. Ward as a Church of England rector in Canberra and a chaplain to the Eighth Brigade, First AIF. This is a transcription of the scrapbook’s attribution, pending external verification.
